BirunIQ · for ArcGIS users

Your ArcGIS, working inside BirunIQ

What an ArcGIS Named User sees in BirunIQ Atlas, on real streets, imagery and FEMA flood zones in Montpelier, Vermont: connect their own account, add Living Atlas layers, style and filter points, lines and polygons, bring in files and any ArcGIS or OGC service, view point clouds and Gaussian splats, and see exactly what their sign-in can read, edit and publish today. "Controlled release" is built and switched off; "coming soon" is not available yet.

COMING SOON TO BIRUNIQ

One engine under everything BirunIQ moves: imagery first, point clouds and splats, then vector data and analytics. Smaller files, less memory and more throughput, so every module and every analysis runs faster.

Codecs and GEOINT · the whole flow

Codecs are the plumbing of geospatial intelligence. Smaller imagery and point clouds move faster from sensor to analyst to map, load faster, and fit in the memory of a server inside an air-gap-capable deployment, so detection, change analysis and the common operating picture all run faster.

What your ArcGIS sign-in can do in BirunIQ

Named User sign-in. Everything goes through BirunIQ's server; ArcGIS permissions decide what you can see and change.

Read: your content, your organisation's, and Living AtlasThrough BirunIQ's proxy; nothing copied; Esri permissions decide.Available today
Edit attributes on hosted feature layersBuilt. A per-organisation switch, off by default.Controlled release
Add features · delete features · change geometryBuilt. No deployment can switch it on until the live test with Esri.Coming soon
Publish a new hosted feature layer from an uploaded datasetTech admin; licence-checked; lineage and the generated mark go in the description.Controlled release
Publish analysis results as a new hosted serviceNot built. Publishing takes an uploaded dataset today.Coming soon

Chapter
Runs about six minutes and loops. Full-screen it for a presentation.
Read, edit and publish, exactlyRead (your content, your organisation's, Living Atlas): available today. Edit attributes on hosted feature layers: built, controlled release (per-organisation switch, off by default). Add, delete and geometry edits: built, coming soon (no deployment can switch them on until the live test with Esri). Publish a new hosted feature layer from an uploaded dataset: built, controlled release. Publish analysis results as a new service: coming soon, not built.
Available today beside ArcGISLiving Atlas search; Shapefile and File Geodatabase upload; ArcGIS feature, map and image services and OGC WMS, WMTS and WFS by URL; styling and filtering points, lines and polygons; LAS and LAZ point clouds, 3D Tiles and Gaussian splats in the 3D Data panel; 3D buildings in the 3D views. The 3D buildings and the Red Rocks splat are recordings of BirunIQ's own renderer. The is coming soon and is not part of BirunIQ yet.
How it stays safeSign-in is OAuth 2.0 with PKCE on the organisation's own ArcGIS page. The BirunIQ server holds the tokens, sends each only to the ArcGIS host that issued it, and never puts one in the browser. ArcGIS permissions decide what each person sees.
About the dataStreets, buildings, rivers and place names: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Flood zones: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (public domain), shown as Esri's Living Atlas layer. Imagery: USGS NAIP Plus (USDA NAIP, public domain). Hydrants, water mains, valves, work orders, the point cloud and the "Example County (demo)" ArcGIS organisation are synthetic demo data placed on the real streets; they are not the City of Montpelier's. No partnership with Esri is claimed.
